content: 1. Dissolve two tablets of citric acid/sodium bicarbonate in water and consume the effervescent solution every four hours as needed. Do not exceed a total of eight tablets within a 24-hour period. Ensure the tablets are fully dissolved in four ounces of water before drinking. 2. For individuals under 12 years of age, the safety and efficacy of citric acid/sodium bicarbonate have not been established. For those aged 12 years and older, dissolve two tablets in water and drink the effervescent solution every four hours as needed, not exceeding eight tablets in 24 hours. Fully dissolve the tablets in four ounces of water before consumption. 3. Adults over 60 years of age should not exceed four tablets of citric acid/sodium bicarbonate within a 24-hour period. 4. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of atazanavir. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, administer atazanavir two hours before or one hour after taking citric acid/sodium bicarbonate. 5. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of baloxavir marboxil by binding to cations in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Studies in monkeys have shown that concurrent use with calcium, aluminum, or iron significantly decreases plasma levels of baloxavir. Human studies have not been conducted. 6. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause premature dissolution, potentially affecting the drug's release properties and absorption in the duodenum. 7. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH, which decreases its solubility and bioavailability. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal tract pH, such as proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), H2 blockers, and antacids, may exacerbate this effect. 8. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH. Ledipasvir's solubility decreases as pH increases, and drugs that raise gastric pH are expected to lower its levels. Separate the administration of antacids and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by at least four hours. 9. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Avoid this interaction by administering antacids two hours before or two hours after nilotinib. 10. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 11. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of pazopanib with drugs that raise gastric pH. Short-acting antacids may be used instead of PPIs and H2 antagonists, but separate antacid and pazopanib dosing by several hours. 12. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Separate pexidartinib administration by two hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. 13. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of riociguat by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by at least one hour. 15. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 16. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. Velpatasvir's solubility decreases as gastric pH increases (it is practically insoluble at pH >5). Separate the administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir from antacids by at least four hours. 17. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate can reduce the effectiveness of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer sotorasib four hours before or ten hours after taking a locally-acting antacid. 18. Discontinue citric acid/sodium bicarbonate if the maximum dosage is taken for two weeks without symptom relief. This medication alters gastric pH and may interfere with the absorption of some concurrent medications. 19. For pregnancy, citric acid/sodium bicarbonate is classified as Category C. It is unknown whether it is distributed in breast milk. Pregnant or breastfeeding patients should consult a healthcare professional before using over-the-counter medications.
